newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber prices soften after deals.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber prices soften after deals.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices softened in noon trading on Thursday after deals in Palembang, traders said.
They said a deal was done at 49.25 U.S. cents/lb fob Palembang for June shipment, which was lower compared with Tuesday's offer price of 49.50. The market was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu holiday.
"Offer prices fell after the Palembang deal. Traders in other cities do not have any choice but to lower the offer prices because buyers will always want to find cheaper rubber," said one trader.
Traders said offer prices fell to 49.75 fob Medan from 50.00 on Tuesday, but many were reluctant to sell at that level.
"Some traders still offer rubber at 50.00 and even 50.25, but I don't think they will succeed in selling goods," said another trader.
Traders said offer prices were quoted at 49.75 fob Surabaya at 49.50 fob Padang and at 49.25 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
"Supply is quite abundant despite wintering in Medan. Nowadays, traders simply ignore the wintering factor because it has failed to boost the prices in many months," said one trader.
